official.deadline_note: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. The Study in Japan official FAQ states that starting dates and deadlines for applications vary by country and region and must be checked with the Japanese embassy or with the official overseas recommending organisation in your own country.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 cycle: MEXT publishes 'COURSES and APPLICATION GUIDELINES for 2027-2028' for the five YLP courses
official.status_note: MEXT's Young Leaders' Program page publishes application guidelines and application forms for the 2027-2028 cycle for all five courses: School of Government and School of Local Governance (hosted by GRIPS), Healthcare Administration (Nagoya University), Business Administration (Hitotsubashi University) and Law (Kyushu University). Recruitment and screening are run by the official overseas recommending organisations and the Japanese embassies in target countries, so the round's timetable differs by country.
benefits: One year of study in a master course at a graduate school in Japan
Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: None for this type
eligibility: You must be under 40 years of age (in principle)
You must be university or college graduates who have practical work experience
Young public administrators, etc. who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries

Recruitment is by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organizations - YLP is neither embassy recommendation nor university recommendation
The type and field of application may differ from country to country, so applicants must check with the Japanese embassy whether there is an opening in the type and field they wish to apply for
As a general rule you must apply from your country of citizenship
requirements: Candidates are recruited through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations
All required documents and interviews are conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission in your country

GRIPS states the programme is open to exceptionally promising young government officials with considerable working experience in public administration, and that in principle a minimum of three years working experience in the field in the applicant's home country is a prerequisite for admission
The latest edition of the application guidelines governs where its contents differ from the portal summary
GRIPS lists, country by country, which authority may recommend for the School of Government and which for the School of Local Governance
documents: The MEXT application form for the specific course applied for - MEXT publishes a separate application form and guideline set for each of the five YLP courses
Recommendation by the official overseas recommending organisation in your country
The documents required by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country, which the official guidance says must be checked with the embassy because requirements vary by country
The documents required by the host graduate school for admission to its master course
selection_criteria: Selection is by the official overseas recommending organisation and the embassy of Japan in the target country

GRIPS admits students on the basis of an appraisal of their potential to become future leaders at home, to play important roles in their countries' development, and to maintain lasting friendship and trust between Japan and other countries
The MEXT YLP Committee set in MEXT conducts the second selection and MEXT makes the final decision
application_method: Obtain a recommendation from the official overseas recommending organisation designated for your country and course
Register with and submit documents to the embassy of Japan in the target country, which conducts the initial screening (documents, interview and essay writing)
MEXT's YLP Committee conducts the second selection and MEXT makes the final decision
Placement is in the master course at the Japanese graduate school hosting the applied course
official.application_route: Nominated by an official overseas recommending organisation, then screened by the Japanese embassy in the target country, then selected by the YLP Committee at MEXT - there is no direct application to MEXT.
official.citizenship_residency: As a general rule you must apply from your country of citizenship, and after passing the examination your student visa must generally be issued in your country of citizenship; return air tickets are as a general rule provided for travel from your country of citizenship to and from Japan.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. GRIPS states the Young Leaders Program scholarship for international students is the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship, and notes a separate YLP Japan route for Japanese applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The course is fixed to the host university and field: School of Government and School of Local Governance (Master of Public Policy at GRIPS), Healthcare Administration (Nagoya University), Business Administration (Hitotsubashi University) and Law (Kyushu University). Only the organisations listed by MEXT and GRIPS for each country may recommend.
official.research_requirement: The GRIPS YLP curriculum includes a final paper based on Independent Study, plus Field Trip/Workshop I-II, for both the School of Government and the School of Local Governance.
official.description: The Young Leaders' Program (YLP) is one of the seven types of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship and aims to cultivate future national leaders in Asian and other countries, to establish friendly relationships among the countries involved and to improve the quality of policy making in the participating countries by forming a network among national leaders. It places young public administrators and other early-career leaders in a one-year master course at a Japanese graduate school, delivered in English at GRIPS for the School of Government and School of Local Governance, with enrolment in October and graduation the following September.
official.program_type: Graduate school level (master course) - Young Leaders Program (YLP) student, one of the seven types of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
official.english_requirement: No MEXT examination subject is listed for YLP in the Study in Japan 'Examinations Required for Embassy Recommendation' table, because YLP is not an embassy-recommendation type. GRIPS publishes 'Language of Instruction: English' for the School of Government and School of Local Governance courses; any language condition comes from the host graduate school and the recommending organisation.

verification.notes: The JPY 242,000 monthly figure, exempted tuition, round-trip airfare, one-year duration, under-40 age rule and the 'official overseas recommending organizations' route were all read directly from the Study in Japan official MEXT scholarship page; the five 2027-2028 courses and their guideline/form sets were read from MEXT's own Young Leaders' Program page, and the English-medium, October-enrolment, Master of Public Policy structure plus the country-by-country list of recommending authorities from GRIPS. No application deadline, study-mode label or full document list is published on any official page - the official FAQ states deadlines vary by country and region.

applicant_utility.summary: YLP is the one MEXT route you cannot enter as an individual: your file has to reach Tokyo through an official overseas recommending authority, so the first job is confirming that your country's designated body actually has a slot for the exact course you want this cycle. The money is strong - JPY 242,000 a month, exempted tuition and round-trip airfare from your country of citizenship - but the entry window is narrow: under 40 in principle, a completed degree, and real public-administration or policy service, with GRIPS treating roughly three years of relevant experience in your home administration as a prerequisite in principle. Five different universities run the five courses, each with its own MEXT application form, so you apply to a specific course, not to 'YLP' in general.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Serving civil servants and young policy professionals under 40 from a YLP target country whose ministry, civil-service commission or designated body appears on the recommending-authority list for their course.
application_readiness_checklist: On the GRIPS YLP page, confirm that your country and your intended course (School of Government versus School of Local Governance) both have a named recommending authority for the current round, then contact that body directly for its internal nomination timetable.
Ask the Japanese embassy in your own country whether your course has seats this cycle, because the embassy runs the screening and local availability of a field differs.

Assemble degree evidence plus a continuous, documented work history in public administration or policy reaching back about three years, since GRIPS treats that length of service as a prerequisite in principle.
Download the MEXT application form and guidelines PDF for your one specific course from MEXT's YLP page - the five courses have separate forms and they are not interchangeable.

Build a study plan that names a concrete policy problem in your home administration rather than a general interest in Japan, because the YLP Committee appraises your potential as a future national leader.
common_rejection_risks: No recommending authority in your country nominates for the course you want, so the file never reaches MEXT at all.
Work history that is too short, too peripheral, or entirely private-sector for a leadership-of-public-administration screening.
Applying from a third country instead of your country of citizenship, which the official FAQ says should be done only as a general rule from the citizenship country.
Submitting another course's application form or an outdated edition of the guidelines, when MEXT says the latest edition governs.
Essay and interview answers that read as Japan enthusiasm rather than a defined leadership role you intend to return to.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: MEXT covers tuition, the JPY 242,000 monthly stipend and round-trip airfare. You still fund your own visa and residence-status costs, any travel to the embassy for screening, personal insurance, dependant costs (family members are not covered by the scholarship), and relocation spending beyond the airfare itself.
document_audit: Certificates of graduation and employment must be originals or copies certified by an authorised official; where photocopies are submitted, official guidance requires certification by the accreditation body or the issuing authority.
Employment certificates must span the whole claimed period of service and be issued by your employing authority, not typed by you.
Each course has its own MEXT form and guideline set - a GRIPS form cannot be used for the Kyushu Law course or the Hitotsubashi Business course.
Your recommending authority will very likely impose its own dated formats and internal cut-off that runs ahead of anything MEXT publishes, so build the file to their template first.
alerts: There is no single central deadline to watch: the recommending authority and the embassy set the timetable, and missing your country's screening usually means waiting a full year.
GRIPS enrols in October and graduates the following September, so do not plan around a Japanese April intake.
The age rule is 'under 40 in principle', so confirm the exact cut-off your recommending authority applies rather than assuming the birthday year.
No preliminary Japanese-language training is provided for YLP, unlike most other MEXT types - you arrive straight into an English-taught master course.
Placement is decided by MEXT, so you apply for a course at a named university but have no guarantee of the campus or elective mix you had in mind.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You are nominated by your country's official overseas recommending authority, screened by the Japanese embassy there on documents, interview and essay, and then selected by the YLP Committee at MEXT, which also fixes your placement.

official.deadline_note: JASSO publishes no deadline for this programme. Applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, so the effective deadline is that school's own pre-arrival admission and internal scholarship nomination cut-off.
official.application_cycle: Two recruitment rounds a year matching the Japanese intake cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October). JASSO published the reference lists of eligible schools and courses for academic year 2026 autumn enrolment in June 2026 and for academic year 2026 spring enrolment in January 2026.
official.status_note: JASSO presents the programme as a standing reservation scheme with two intakes a year, and lists the recognised schools, departments and courses for the 2026 spring and 2026 autumn intakes as reference material. The 2027 intake lists have not yet been posted on the page; the next set is expected on the same annual pattern. Recruiting itself is done by each eligible school, so the live round is the school's nomination round.
benefits: Monthly stipend of 48,000 yen per month (the amount may change from one academic year to another)
Scholarship period for students enrolled in April: 12 months (from April in the year of enrolment to the following March)
Scholarship period for students enrolled in September or October: 6 months (from October in the year of enrolment to the following March)
eligibility: Privately-financed international student who has received pre-arrival admission and faces financial difficulties, with an excellent academic and character record
Plans to enrol as a full-time student in a graduate school in Japan in April (September or October for autumn enrolment) using pre-arrival admission - graduate level reservation category

Plans to enrol as a full-time student in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd grade or upper) or specialized course in a specialized training college in Japan in April (September or October for autumn enrolment) using pre-arrival admission - EJU exam or English courses reservation categories
'Full-time student' under this program does not include research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students
requirements: JASSO does not accept applications directly from students; the procedure must be completed through the school the applicant plans to enrol in

The school must be an eligible recommending school for the relevant reservation category: graduate level (graduate schools offering pre-arrival admission), EJU exam (schools registered with JASSO as offering pre-arrival admission using EJU, excluding graduate schools) or English courses (undergraduate courses providing degrees or associate degrees with classes conducted only in English, excluding graduate schools)

For the EJU exam reservation category, JASSO uses the list of registered schools as of 1 October 2025 for spring enrolment and as of 1 April 2026 for September or October enrolment, which do not necessarily equal the list published on the page
To receive the scholarship, the candidate must complete the procedure through the school
documents: JASSO publishes no document list for this programme; the required documents are those set by the enrolling school for its reservation nomination
selection_criteria: Awarded to privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are facing financial difficulties
JASSO's stated objectives are to contribute to ease their financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, to promote pre-arrival admission and to improve the level of learning
The practical selection is carried out by the school through its reservation nomination
coverage: Monthly stipend of 48,000 yen per month
12 months of support for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March)
6 months of support for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
application_method: Ask the school you plan to enrol in - JASSO states that applications from students directly are not accepted
The school makes the reservation nomination for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship
JASSO publishes the reservation categories and the lists of eligible schools, departments and courses for each intake
official.application_route: Obtain pre-arrival admission from a school on JASSO's eligible list for your reservation category, then ask that school to make the nomination; JASSO will not accept an application from you directly.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to privately-financed international students admitted by pre-arrival admission; JASSO publishes no nationality or country-of-residence restriction on this page.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is defined as being for privately-financed international students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted by reservation category: graduate level for graduate schools offering pre-arrival admission; EJU exam for schools registered with JASSO as offering pre-arrival admission using EJU, excluding graduate schools; English courses for undergraduate courses that award a degree or associate degree with classes conducted only in English, excluding graduate schools.
official.duration: 12 months for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March); 6 months for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
official.description: JASSO's reservation programme designates privately-financed international students who have received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese graduate school, undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (third year or above) or specialized course in a specialized training college, and who face financial difficulties, as reservists of the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship. Its stated purpose is to ease their financial concerns about arriving and studying in Japan, to promote pre-arrival admission and to raise the level of learning, and it pays a monthly stipend for the first year of enrolment.
official.region: Japan-based; JASSO publishes no country or region restriction
official.program_type: Reservation programme of the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, by pre-arrival admission school recommendation

verification.notes: The JPY 48,000 monthly stipend, the 12-month and 6-month periods, the three reservation categories, the pre-arrival admission definition, the exclusions from 'full-time student' and the school-only application route were all read directly from JASSO's own English page for this programme, cross-checked against the Japanese edition of the same page. JASSO publishes no deadline, no tuition exemption, no language test and no document list for this programme; the amount is stated as liable to change from one academic year to another.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to JASSO for this yourself - the school that has given you pre-arrival admission runs the recommendation, so your first move is to email that school's international student office and ask whether it is a JASSO-eligible recommending institution for your reservation category and intake. If they nominate you and you enrol, the money is JPY 48,000 a month, running 12 months from April for an April enrolment but only 6 months from October if you enrol in September or October, and JASSO warns the figure can change from one academic year to the next. Treat it as a living-cost bridge for your first months in Japan rather than a funding package, since JASSO publishes no tuition exemption and no airfare for this scheme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-financed international students who already hold or are about to receive pre-arrival admission from a JASSO-listed Japanese school and need a first-year cash cushion before they can earn in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask your admitting school in writing whether it is on JASSO's eligible list for the category you fall into - graduate level, EJU exam, or English courses - for your specific intake, and whether it has a nomination slot free at all.

Check JASSO's published school, department and course lists for your intake year; the 2026 autumn lists went up in June 2026 and the 2026 spring lists in January 2026, and JASSO labels them as reference.

If your admission is EJU-based, verify your school against JASSO's registered pre-arrival admission list using EJU, because JASSO works from the 1 October 2025 snapshot for spring and the 1 April 2026 snapshot for autumn, which may not match the page.
Confirm in writing that you will be a regular full-time degree student, not a research student, trainee, non-degree, advanced-course, special-course, auditing or special student.
Prepare evidence of financial difficulty and your academic and character records in whatever format that school's scholarship nomination requires, since JASSO sets no form of its own.
common_rejection_risks: Your school is not a JASSO-eligible recommending institution for your category or intake, so no nomination can be made no matter how strong your file is.
The school has used up its recommendation capacity for the year, which JASSO notes varies by school.
Your admission is to a research, non-degree, auditing or special-student status rather than a regular degree course.
You miss the school's internal nomination cut-off, which typically sits months before you arrive and is invisible from outside the institution.
Your admitted course or department is not on the recognised list for that intake, so the nomination does not line up with the award.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Enrolment fee, tuition, airfare to Japan, accommodation deposits and initial set-up costs, and the gap between JPY 48,000 a month and actual living costs in Tokyo or Osaka are all yours to fund - JASSO's reservation programme pays only the monthly stipend.
document_audit: There is no JASSO form to fill in: the document set is whatever the school's scholarship office asks for, so request their list as early as possible and in English.
Your pre-arrival admission letter must name the exact course and intake that appears on the eligible list, otherwise the nomination will not match.
Keep your EJU result certificate to hand if you are admitted through the EJU route, because JASSO's EJU lists are keyed to EJU-based pre-arrival admission.
Never send anything to JASSO directly - applications from students are not accepted and will not be actioned.
alerts: There is no JASSO deadline for you to diarise; the controlling date is the school's own pre-arrival admission and internal nomination cut-off.
The stipend is tied to the academic year and JASSO says it may change, so treat JPY 48,000 as indicative for a future intake rather than guaranteed.
An autumn (September or October) enrolment receives only 6 months of payment ending the following March, compared with 12 months for an April enrolment - the same award is worth half as much.

The English courses category is defined by the degree being taught only in English, not by your test score, so a school that mixes Japanese-taught classes will not qualify for that category even if the degree is nominally in English.

This is a reservation of the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship, so it sits inside a first-year framework; continuing support beyond the reservation period depends on re-applying through the school after you arrive.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure pre-arrival admission from an eligible school, ask that school to run the internal reservation nomination to JASSO, and receive the stipend from your enrolment month for the stated period.
